questions.q: What type of tissue is the epidermis, and is it vascular?
options: Simple cuboidal epithelium with many capillaries
Stratified squamous keratinised epithelium with no blood vessels
questions.explain: It is nourished by diffusion from dermal capillaries.

open.q: What type of tissue is the epidermis, and is it vascular?

questions.q: Name the strata of the epidermis from deep to superficial.
questions.explain: Cells migrate upwards from the basal layer, keratinise and are shed.

open.q: Name the strata of the epidermis from deep to superficial.

questions.q: Which epidermal layer is present only in thick skin (palms and soles)?
questions.explain: It is a thin, clear layer between the granulosum and the corneum.

open.q: Which epidermal layer is present only in thick skin (palms and soles)?

questions.q: Which epidermal layer contains actively dividing cells?

open.q: Which epidermal layer contains actively dividing cells?

questions.q: In which epidermal layer are melanocytes mainly found?
questions.explain: They are derived from the neural crest and transfer melanin to keratinocytes.

open.q: In which epidermal layer are melanocytes mainly found?

questions.q: What is the function of Langerhans cells?
questions.explain: They capture antigens in the epidermis and carry them to lymph nodes.

open.q: What is the function of Langerhans cells?

questions.q: What is the function of Merkel cells?
options: They act as touch receptors in the basal epidermis
questions.explain: They are associated with sensory nerve endings.

open.q: What is the function of Merkel cells?

questions.q: What is the superficial layer of the dermis called?
questions.explain: It forms dermal papillae that interlock with the epidermis. The deeper reticular layer is dense irregular connective tissue.

open.q: What is the superficial layer of the dermis called?

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explain: UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol in the epidermis.

open.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight?

questions.q: Which precursor in the skin is converted to cholecalciferol by UV light?
questions.explain: Cholecalciferol is then hydroxylated in the liver and kidney.

open.q: Which precursor in the skin is converted to cholecalciferol by UV light?

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of the skin?
questions.explain: Insulin is made by the pancreas.

questions.q: Which nerve fibres supply eccrine sweat glands?
questions.explain: This is an exception: sympathetic postganglionic fibres that release acetylcholine.

open.q: Which nerve fibres supply eccrine sweat glands?

questions.q: Where are apocrine sweat glands mainly found?
questions.explain: They become active at puberty. Bacterial breakdown of their secretion causes body odour.

open.q: Where are apocrine sweat glands mainly found?

questions.q: By what mechanism do sebaceous glands release their secretion?
questions.explain: The whole cell breaks down and is released as sebum.

open.q: By what mechanism do sebaceous glands release their secretion?

questions.q: Which skin areas have no sebaceous glands?
questions.explain: Most sebaceous glands open into hair follicles.

open.q: Which skin areas have no sebaceous glands?

questions.q: Compared with plasma, is sweat hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic?
questions.explain: Primary sweat is isotonic, but NaCl is reabsorbed in the duct.

open.q: Compared with plasma, is sweat hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic?

questions.q: What is raised in sweat in cystic fibrosis?
questions.explain: Defective CFTR stops chloride reabsorption in the sweat duct, which is the basis of the sweat test.

open.q: What is raised in sweat in cystic fibrosis?

questions.q: Sebum production is stimulated by which hormones?
questions.explain: This is why acne begins at puberty.

open.q: Sebum production is stimulated by which hormones?
